review.material: Author-hosted original inspected for rational coordinates, line representation, Boolean algorithms and data structures; printed pp. 470–471 also checked as page images.
review.limitations: The pseudocode was read for its structure, not independently implemented or formally verified. Operation-count bounds are not modern machine benchmarks.

evidence.description: Defines exact rational coordinates and ordered maximal-line lists.
Derives union, difference, intersection, parthood and equality procedures.
Explains ordered-list/tree organization and implementation routines.

sections.title: In brief
sections.text: Krishnamurti turns shape arithmetic into algorithms: combine line content, remove it, keep common intervals, test parthood and compare shapes. The emphasis is choosing a representation that makes geometric coverage computable.

sections.title: The question
sections.text: How can a program manipulate shapes geometrically, including parts that were never separate drawing objects, without relying on approximate coordinate equality?

sections.title: Main idea or claim
sections.text: Exact rational coordinates and maximal-line organization support systematic Boolean operations on shapes and labelled shapes. Drawing order is replaced by geometric ordering.

sections.title: How the work approaches it
sections.text: Group collinear maximal segments by their supporting-line descriptor, then order their endpoints. Compare compatible lists with advancing scans; handle labelled points through corresponding set operations. Later routines organize updates with linked lists and balanced trees.

sections.title: Evidence and examples
sections.text: The paper supplies pseudocode, correctness arguments and interval-case diagrams. Figure 5 distinguishes shortening, splitting and deleting a line during subtraction; Figure 6 gives the corresponding intersections.

sections.title: What comes out of it
sections.text: For already ordered, same-carrier lists, union, difference and intersection have linear operation-count bounds in the combined list lengths. These local bounds should not be read as a universal bound for unrestricted rule matching.

sections.title: Limits to keep in mind
sections.text: This is analytical algorithm development, not a user experiment or timing study. Rational line shapes and labelled points are the stated setting; finding the transformations for rule application is pursued in the 1981 companion paper.

sections.title: What to take from it
sections.text: Think coverage and maximal segments rather than original strokes. Read representation first, then trace subtraction on two overlapping intervals before tackling the implementation data structures.
